candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And the third was named Gadreel: he it is who showed the children of men all the blows of death, and he led astray Eve, and showed the weapons of death to the sons of men, the shield and the coat of mail, and the sword for battle, and all the weapons of death to the children of men' — Gadreel as the angel who taught violence. Tewahedo pacifist-monastic tradition (the demand that monks bear no weapon) cites this verse as the canonical condemnation of weapons-craft at its angelic origin: violence is not natural to creation, it was TAUGHT by a fallen angel.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And by that oath the heaven was suspended before the world was created and for ever. And through it the earth was founded upon the water' — the cosmogonic Oath. Tewahedo wisdom tradition reads this as the textual root for the sacramental power of the divine Name: just as the Oath holds the cosmos together, the invocation of the Name in liturgy holds the worshipping community together. The Sǝbḫata Foṣǝlt invokes this directly.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And he sat on the throne of his glory, and the sum of judgment was given unto the Son of Man, and he caused the sinners to pass away and be destroyed from off the face of the earth, and those who have led the world astray' — Son of Man enthroned at consummation, parallel and prior to Jn 5:22-27. Tewahedo Christology cites this as the textual basis for the doctrine that the Father has GIVEN judgment to the Son — not delegated provisionally, but transferred completely.
